blocks.source: Vol IV, The Cognitive Brain, § Chunk Supply and Evidence Validity
blocks.md: One INT4 evaluation of the intent model takes …. Over that interval the mug keeps riding the conveyor, and an arm tracking a new setpoint every few tens of milliseconds would have nothing to track if each proposal named a single setpoint. Predicting a sequence of setpoints per evaluation solves the supply problem but raises a second one that the memory wall never touched. Every setpoint in such a sequence descends from one observation, so the sequence can outlast the evidence behind it.

questions.q: The section **Chunk Supply and Evidence Validity** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: At batch size 1 a proposer streams every weight once per fresh evaluation, so its renewal rate is bounded by sustained bandwidth over weight bytes (14 GB at 142.8 GB/s is 98 ms per sweep, about 10 Hz before vision or decoding).

Predicting H setpoints per evaluation divides weight traffic per supplied setpoint by H, but it leaves reaction latency at one renewal period plus one inference, so chunking supplies setpoints without refreshing them.

Every setpoint in a chunk descends from one capture, so a chunk is valid only while extrapolated target drift stays inside the tolerance margin (about 219 ms for the tracked mug against a 60 ms untracked deadline), and supply and validity are separate budgets.

The permission path can refuse only claims it can compare with its own evidence, so an interface that passes a latent vector or a language subtask cannot be grounded or aged, while a geometric payload can.
